subject: Applied Calculus

sourceBasis.syllabus: R-2025 Unit IV: iterated integrals/Fubini, double integrals, change of order, Cartesian and polar coordinates, triple integrals, and Cartesian/cylindrical/spherical coordinate systems.

note: Original ACADRIX 1-mark practice questions; not claimed official Anna University questions or verified PYQs.

questions.q: What is a double integral?
questions.a: An integral that accumulates a quantity over a two-dimensional region.

questions.q: What is a triple integral?
questions.a: An integral that accumulates a quantity throughout a three-dimensional volume.

questions.q: What is an iterated integral?
questions.a: A multiple integral evaluated through successive single integrations.

questions.q: What is the basic idea of Fubini's theorem?
questions.a: Under suitable conditions, a multiple integral can be evaluated as an iterated integral.

questions.q: In dy dx, which variable is integrated first?
In dx dy, which variable is integrated first?
What is the Cartesian area element?
questions.a: dA=dx dy, or equivalently dy dx.

questions.q: What is the Cartesian volume element?
questions.a: dV=dx dy dz in the chosen order.

questions.q: What does ∬R f(x,y)dA represent?
questions.a: The accumulated value of f over the region R.

questions.q: What does a double integral of 1 over a planar region represent?
What does a triple integral of 1 over a solid represent?
What does a triple integral of a volume density represent?
questions.a: The total mass when the integrand is the volume density.

questions.q: What does changing the order of integration mean geometrically?
questions.a: Describing the same region using a different sequence of integration.

questions.q: Can the limits usually remain unchanged when the order of integration is changed?
questions.a: No; the limits generally must be reconstructed from the same region.

questions.q: What should be identified before changing the order of a double integral?
questions.a: The geometric region and its boundary curves.

questions.q: Why is a sketch useful when changing the order of integration?
questions.a: It reveals the region's boundaries and helps determine the new limits.

questions.q: What are Cartesian coordinates convenient for?
questions.a: Rectangles, boxes, straight-line boundaries and regions naturally expressed in x, y and z.

questions.q: Write the polar transformation for x.
Write the polar transformation for y.
In polar coordinates, what is x²+y²?
Write the polar area element.
What is the Jacobian factor in the polar area element?
Why does the factor r appear in polar area integration?
questions.a: It accounts for the change in area under the coordinate transformation.

questions.q: Which coordinate system is natural for a circular disk?
What are typical polar limits for a full disk of radius a?
What should be determined first when choosing polar limits?
questions.a: The angular range from the rays, symmetry or boundary geometry.

questions.q: What is the radial coordinate r in polar coordinates?
What is the angular coordinate θ in polar coordinates?
questions.a: The angle specifying the direction from the positive x-axis in the standard convention.

questions.q: What is a Jacobian in coordinate transformation?
questions.a: A factor that accounts for the change in area or volume under a change of variables.

questions.q: What are cylindrical coordinates an extension of?
questions.a: Polar coordinates extended into three dimensions.

questions.q: Write the cylindrical transformation for x.
Write the cylindrical transformation for y.
What happens to z in cylindrical coordinates?
Write the cylindrical volume element.
Which coordinate system is especially useful for a cylinder about the z-axis?
In cylindrical coordinates, what does r represent?
What is the usual θ range for a full revolution about the z-axis?
What are spherical coordinates suited to?
questions.a: Spheres, spherical shells and solids with radial symmetry about the origin.

questions.q: Write the spherical transformation for x.
Write the spherical transformation for y.
Write the spherical transformation for z.
Write the spherical volume element.
What is ρ in spherical coordinates?
questions.a: The radial distance from the origin.

questions.q: What is θ in the spherical-coordinate convention used here?
questions.a: The azimuthal angle in the xy-plane.

questions.q: What is φ in the spherical-coordinate convention used here?
questions.a: The angle measured from the positive z-axis.

questions.q: What are the limits for a full sphere of radius a in spherical coordinates?
Which Jacobian factor is essential in spherical volume integration?
Which coordinate system is generally best for a region bounded mainly by straight Cartesian planes?
Which coordinate system is generally best for a solid with circular symmetry around the z-axis?
Which coordinate system is generally best for a solid with spherical symmetry about the origin?
What is the main principle for choosing a coordinate system?
questions.a: Choose the system that makes the boundary, limits and Jacobian simplest.

questions.q: What is the first practical step in evaluating a triple integral over a complicated solid?
questions.a: Identify and, where possible, sketch the solid.

questions.q: In what direction are iterated integrals normally evaluated?
What must be included when converting a double integral to polar coordinates?
questions.a: The transformed integrand, new limits and the Jacobian factor r in dA.

questions.q: What must be included when converting a triple integral to spherical coordinates?
questions.a: The transformed integrand, spherical limits and the Jacobian factor ρ²sinφ.
